Fix critter decode building a new Conversions per property (#4338)

## Problem
Critter-mapped entities decoded about 10× slower than reflective ones
and allocated about 15× more per decode. The new mapper benchmarks
(#4336) surfaced this.

JFR showed almost all the time and allocation inside
`Conversions.<init>`, called from `PropertyModel.setValue`:

```java
Conversions c = conversions != null ? conversions
        : new Conversions(Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader());
```

Reflective property models get `.conversions(mapper.getConversions())`
from `FieldDiscovery` / `MethodDiscovery`. Critter's generated property
models never had it set. Every property set during decode therefore
rebuilt the whole conversions registry: a few dozen map entries and
lambdas.

## Fix
`CritterEntityModel.configureProperties(mapper)` now also sets
`property.conversions(mapper.getConversions())`. That method already
runs at the end of every generated entity-model constructor, AOT and
runtime alike. Existing AOT output picks up the fix without
regeneration.

## Results
In-memory JMH benchmarks from #4336, JDK 21, short warmed runs:

| decode | reflection | critter before | critter after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| SIMPLE | 2.6 µs, 3,080 B/op | 25 µs, 46,089 B/op | 2.4 µs, 3,144 B/op
|
| NESTED | 12.1 µs, 28,944 B/op | 62 µs, 136,562 B/op | 12.0 µs, 28,864
B/op |

COLLECTIONS, POLYMORPHIC and LIFECYCLE also now match reflection for
both critter AOT and critter runtime. Encode was never affected.

## Testing
- Full `morphia-core` suite (Testcontainers MongoDB 8.0.0):
- `-Dmorphia.mapper=critter`: 1,274 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 17
skipped.
- `-Dmorphia.mapper=reflection`: 1,274 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 17
skipped.
- `spotless:apply` makes no changes.

Create the critter class loader lazily and drop its ByteBuddy base class (#4344)

## Problem

After #4342 and #4343, every benchmark model loads from AOT, but
critter's `coldStart` was still about 12% slower than reflection. The
cause was `CritterMapper`'s constructor, which always creates a
`CritterClassLoader`, even when every model is pre-generated and the
loader is never used.

`CritterClassLoader` extended ByteBuddy's
`ByteArrayClassLoader.ChildFirst`, so creating one initialized a large
part of ByteBuddy on every cold start. Diffing the classes loaded by a
cold `mappedMapper` call against reflection showed 79 ByteBuddy classes,
plus JDK dynamic proxies and classes like `Process`, `Console` and
`ResourceBundle` that nothing else needs. Constructing a
`CritterClassLoader` alone cost about 43–60 ms in a fresh JVM.

## Fix

- **Lazy loader:** `CritterMapper` creates its `CritterClassLoader` the
first time a model has to be generated at runtime. Copies of a mapper
share one holder, so they still share one loader.
- **No ByteBuddy base class:** `CritterClassLoader` is now a plain
`ClassLoader`. It keeps the behavior that generated code relies on:
- registered classes and `dev.morphia.critter.*` classes load
child-first; everything else goes to the parent
- a class's bytes are released once it is defined, as with ByteBuddy's
default `LATENT` persistence
- `getResource`/`getResourceAsStream` return `null` for the `.class`
file of a registered or child-defined class; `getResources` still lists
the parent's copy, as before

ByteBuddy is still a dependency because `ReferenceCodec` uses it for
lazy reference proxies.

`CritterClassLoaderTest` pins this contract. I wrote it first and
confirmed it passes against the old ByteBuddy-based loader, then against
the new one.

One behavior change: the no-arg-loader constructor used to pass the
`CritterClassLoader` to `AbstractMapper` as the mapper's class loader,
which is used for `Conversions`, `DiscriminatorLookup` and package
scanning. It now passes the context class loader directly. Most classes
resolve the same way, because the old loader delegated them to the
parent. `dev.morphia.critter.*` classes looked up by name are the
exception: the old loader would have returned a second copy of those,
distinct from the mapped class.

## Results

JMH `MappingBenchmark.coldStart`, 20 forks:

| | master | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| critter | 224.8 ± 8.1 ms | **197.5 ± 4.5 ms** |
| critter-runtime | 241.4 ± 5.3 ms | 229.6 ± 19.1 ms |
| reflection | 133.8 ± 4.1 ms | n/a |

On master alone most of the critter gap is the types that still fall
back to runtime generation, which #4342 and #4343 fix. With all three
changes combined, critter's `coldStart` measured 125.4 ± 1.5 ms against
128.6 ± 2.7 ms for reflection. A control run without the lazy loader
measured 160.9 ± 16.8 ms. That combined measurement used the lazy loader
with the old ByteBuddy base class; once the loader is never created, the
base class makes no difference there.

## Testing

- New `CritterClassLoaderTest`: passes against both the old and new
loader.
- Full `morphia-core` suite with regenerated AOT test models and
`-Dmorphia.mapper=critter`: 1279 run, 0 failures. The 33 AOT-skipped
test entities go through runtime generation, so this exercises the new
loader.
- Full `morphia-core` suite with `-Dmorphia.mapper=reflection`: 1279
run, 0 failures.
- critter-maven unit tests (5) and invoker ITs (3) pass.

Test critter's pre-generated models in pull-request CI (#4370)

Adds a **Critter (AOT)** job to the Pull Requests workflow, so pull
requests exercise critter's pre-generated models and not only runtime
generation.

### Why
- **Today's PR job:** the shared workflow behind `Build` runs a plain
`install -Dmorphia.mapper=critter`. Core's build doesn't run
critter-maven, so there are no pre-generated models and critter
generates every model at runtime. That's how #4366's AOT record tests
failed in PR CI.
- **Push builds:** branches pushed to this repo also run `build.yml`.
That workflow generates the models and tests against them, so same-repo
PRs did get AOT coverage there.
- **Forks:** pull requests from forks only run this workflow, so they
never tested the AOT path.

### What the job does
It mirrors `build.yml`:
1. `install -DskipTests`
2. `generate-test-models` in `core`
3. `surefire:test -Dmorphia.mapper=critter`, which doesn't recompile.
Recompiling would replace the woven classes and leave stale models
(`NoSuchMethodError: __readXxx`).

The existing `Build` job is unchanged. It keeps running critter with
runtime generation for every model, which, together with `Coverage
Report (critter)` in `build.yml`, is the only full-suite run of the
runtime tier. The two jobs cover the two critter tiers.

### Verified locally
- The workflow parses.
- I ran the job's three commands as written: `BUILD SUCCESS` across the
reactor.
- Core ran 1313 tests against the generated models (0 failures, 16
skipped). The `Aot*` record fixtures got their models, and their
AOT-tier checks passed.

This PR's own CI runs the new job, since `pull_request` uses the
workflow from the PR.

The new job isn't a required check. If it should block merges, add
`Critter (AOT)` to master's required status checks.

Fixes #4369

Cache entity codecs in a ConcurrentHashMap (plan item 2.8) (#4397)

Plan item **2.8** (review D8). This completes the Phase 2 fixes. 2.5
ships with 3.8, as the plan says.

## The bug
`MorphiaCodecProvider.codecs` was a plain `HashMap`, and `get` mutated
it on every miss. With concurrent first use of an entity type, a
`HashMap` can be corrupted. Even when it isn't, every thread that missed
built its own `MorphiaCodec` and stored it, overwriting the others, so
callers ended up holding different codec instances for the same type.

## Change
`codecs` is a `ConcurrentHashMap`. On a miss, `get` builds the codec and
stores it with `putIfAbsent`. If another thread stored one first, it
returns that one, so every caller shares a single codec per type.

It doesn't use `computeIfAbsent`, as the plan says: building a codec
looks up other codecs, and those lookups can land back in this provider,
which isn't allowed inside a `ConcurrentHashMap` compute.

## Tests
`CodecHarnessTest.concurrentCodecLookupsShareOneCodec` runs under both
mappers. For 20 fresh providers, 8 threads released together call
`provider.get(HarnessScalars.class, registry)`, and the test asserts
that all of them get the same codec. It failed before the fix:
*"REFLECTION: every lookup should get the one cached codec"*.

The core and Kotlin suites pass with `-Dmorphia.mapper=critter` and with
reflection: 1483 + 5 tests, 0 failures.

## Decisions to review
1. **Recursive self-lookups now keep the inner codec.** If building a
type's codec recursively looks up that same type, the inner lookup
stores its codec first, and the outer one is discarded. Before, the
outer one overwrote it. Both are fully built codecs for the same model.
